questions.question: How many equilateral triangles can a regular hexagon be divided into?
questions.explanation: A regular hexagon divides into exactly 6 equilateral triangles by joining each vertex to the centre O.

questions.question: What is the measure of each angle of an equilateral triangle?
questions.explanation: All three angles are equal to 60° because 180° ÷ 3 = 60°.

questions.question: Why do 6 equilateral triangles fit perfectly around the centre?
questions.explanation: Each triangle contributes 60° at centre. 6 × 60° = 360° — they fit with no gaps.

questions.question: What is the interior angle at each vertex of a regular hexagon?
questions.explanation: Two triangle angles meet at each vertex: 60° + 60° = 120°.

questions.question: To construct a regular hexagon, the compass radius should be:
questions.explanation: Compass radius = circle radius creates equilateral triangles with 60° arcs.

questions.question: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
questions.explanation: 6 lines of mirror symmetry — 3 through opposite vertices and 3 through midpoints.

questions.question: Why can regular hexagons tile the plane without gaps?
questions.explanation: 3 interior angles of 120° meet: 3 × 120° = 360°. Perfect coverage.

questions.question: What is the rotational symmetry order of a regular hexagon?
questions.explanation: 6-fold rotational symmetry. Identical after every 60° rotation (360° ÷ 6).

description: A fully responsive interactive tool that shows how a regular hexagon is composed of 6 equilateral triangles and guides students through constructing one using 60-degree angles. Learn mode has 5 animated steps with slow triangle placement in steps 2-3. Practice mode is MCQ-only (no diagrams) with 8 questions, score tracking, and results screen. Uses Singularity Design System (Poppins font, #4A4DC9 primary, #FF7212 accent, #533086→#FC9145 gradient). Layout adapts from desktop side-by-side to mobile stacked via ResizeObserver container queries.
teaching_notes: The equilateral triangle is the building block — its 60-degree angle is what makes the hexagon work. Steps 2 and 3 use slowed-down animations (1.2s per triangle, 0.45s stagger) so students can observe each triangle being placed one at a time. Emphasise that the compass radius equals the circle radius for the construction, which automatically gives 60-degree arcs. Connect to the tiling section: hexagons tile the plane because their interior angle (120 degrees) divides 360 degrees evenly (3 × 120 = 360). Practice mode uses text-only MCQs without diagrams to test conceptual understanding independently.

tool_objectives.instructions_for_student: A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides and 6 equal angles. We will show how it is made of 6 equilateral triangles arranged around a centre point O.
Watch as equilateral triangles are placed slowly around the centre. Each contributes 60° at the centre. After 3 triangles: 3 × 60° = 180° (half circle).
All 6 triangles fit perfectly: 6 × 60° = 360° with no gaps. The interior angle at each hexagon vertex is 60° + 60° = 120°.
Now construct the hexagon: draw a circle, place one vertex, then use the compass (set to the radius) to step around the circle marking 60° arcs for each new vertex.
The regular hexagon is complete! Notice its 6-fold rotational symmetry — it looks identical after every 60° rotation. It also has 6 lines of mirror symmetry.

instructions_for_student: Explore how 6 equilateral triangles form a regular hexagon, then construct one using compass-and-straightedge 60-degree angle marking. Watch the triangles appear one by one in steps 2 and 3 to see how they fit. Then test your understanding with 8 MCQ questions in Practice mode.
